name: Asa
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Jehoshaphat the son of Asa begins to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, at thirty-five years old, and reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. He walks in the ways of Asa his father, doing right in the eyes of the Lord, though the high places are not taken away and the people still burn incense there.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The kings of Judah are set down in order from Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and on through the line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: Abijah sleeps with his fathers and Asa his son reigns; the land is quiet ten years. Asa does that which is good and right, taking away the altars of the strange gods, the high places, the images, and the groves.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

points: Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

points: The Most High smites the Ethiopians before Asa; they flee and are destroyed, and Judah carries away very much spoil. Faith in the Most High, not the numbers of the enemy, wins the battle.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

points: The Spirit of God comes on Azariah the son of Oded, who meets Asa and says the Most High is with them while they are with him; if they seek him he will be found, but if they forsake him he will forsake them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 15: The Covenant to Seek the Most High

points: When Asa hears these words and the prophecy of Oded, he takes courage, puts away the abominable idols out of Judah, Benjamin, and the cities he took from mount Ephraim, and renews the altar of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 15: The Covenant to Seek the Most High

points: Asa removes Maachah his mother from being queen because she made an idol in a grove; he cuts it down, stamps it, and burns it at the brook Kidron.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 15: The Covenant to Seek the Most High

points: Though the high places are not all taken away, the heart of Asa is perfect all his days. He brings the dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of God, and there is no more war until the thirty and fifth year of his reign.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 15: The Covenant to Seek the Most High

points: In the six and thirtieth year of Asa, Baasha king of Israel comes up against Judah and builds Ramah to keep any from going out or coming in to Asa.
Baasha is trying to stop the northern kingdom from coming down to Judah, because tribes out of Israel had been turning their hearts back to the Most High and joining Asa.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: Instead of crying to the Most High as he did against Zerah, Asa takes silver and gold out of the house of the Lord and the king's house and hires Benhadad king of Syria to break his league with Baasha.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: Benhadad smites the cities of Israel, so Baasha leaves off building Ramah. Asa carries away the stones and timber of Ramah and builds Geba and Mizpah with them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: Hanani the seer comes to Asa and rebukes him for relying on the king of Syria and not on the Most High, so the host of Syria has escaped his hand. Had he relied on the Most High, he would have delivered them as he did the Ethiopians.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: so he had a disease in his feet. Yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians. So who you got to seek first and foremost when you sick? You got to go to the Lord, not the physician first. This brother, he did not go to the Lord; he went to the physicians first.

note.label: FDA: Food And Drug Assassination

points: In the thirty and ninth year of his reign Asa is diseased in his feet, exceeding great, yet he seeks not to the Most High but to the physicians. The rebuke is not against physicians but against seeking them in place of the Most High, from whom healing cometh.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: He placed forces and garrisons in the fenced cities of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa had taken.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

points: There came a writing to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet, telling him he had not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat his father nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, but in the way of the kings of Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

points: The pit Ishmael filled with the slain was the one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel during the war between them.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

cases.name: Asa in his first years
cases.charge: Taking away the altars of the strange gods, the high places, the images and the groves; commanding Judah to seek the Lord and to do the law; crying to the Lord against a thousand thousand Ethiopians
cases.preview: Asa son of Abijah, one of the better kings to reign in Judah, took away the strange altars, high places, images and groves, and commanded Judah to seek the Lord and do the law (2 Chronicles 14:1-5).

cases.name: Asa in his latter years
cases.charge: Relying on the king of Syria and not on the Lord; putting the seer in a prison house for the rebuke; in his disease seeking not to the Lord, but to the physicians
